title: Fire That Consumes Fire
subtitle: Zohar, Parashat Yitro, II 89b (part 3) · Rabbi Yehoshua Weitzman
summary: The Torah forbids all labor on the Sabbath, yet it singles out one: “You shall kindle no fire in all your dwellings on the Sabbath day” (Exodus 35:3). Rabbi Shimon explains that fire is judgment (din), and the Sabbath is a day on which Atika Kadisha, the Holy Ancient One, is revealed, when no judgment is seen. Kindling fire contradicts the very essence of the day.

Why, then, is fire lit on the altar? Because that fire is of another kind: “a fire that consumes fire.” It is not itself judgment; it subdues and sweetens judgment. Following the Ramak, Rabbi Weitzman explains that Atika is revealed through Binah, the root of the judgments. Cut off from its source, fire is harsh judgment; joined to its source, it sweetens and elevates.

The Leshem (Rabbi Shlomo Elyashiv) explains the language of eating. Every clarification (berur), in all the worlds, is called “eating”: food is taken in, the waste is separated and the pure part ascends. In the body this is done by the natural heat. In the same way the holy fire consumes the husks and raises the sparks of holiness. Human labor, such as sowing, does this as well.

Finally, the verse says “six days Hashem made,” not “in six days.” The days are not a measure of time; they are the six sefirot of Zeir Anpin, in which the Holy Name is included. From the Leshem's Hakdamot u-She'arim, Rabbi Weitzman adds that the word “made” is said of Atzilut too, for there the hidden emerges from potential into actuality.
terms: “The Holy Ancient One,” in whose revelation there is no judgment
Softening judgment by joining it to its source
“Understanding,” the sefirah that is the root of the judgments
“Strength,” the sefirah of judgment and its forces
The configuration of the six sefirot from Chesed to Yesod
“Splendor,” the central sefirah of Zeir Anpin
Clarification: sifting the good from the waste and raising it
The world of Emanation; the three worlds below it (Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah)

cues.text: Rabbi Shimon also said:
“It is written: ‘Kindle no fire in all your dwellings on the Sabbath day.’
Why? So that judgment should not be seen on this day.
And if you say: but it does ascend to the Most High?
‘In all your dwellings,’ it says, and not to the Most High.
And what does ascend to the Most High ascends to subdue another judgment.
As we learned: there is a fire that consumes fire,
and the fire of the altar consumes another fire.
Therefore the Holy Ancient One (Atika Kadisha) is
revealed on this day more than on all other days.
And when the Ancient One is revealed, no judgment is seen at all;
all those above and below are found in perfect joy, and judgment does not rule.
We learned: it is written, ‘For six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth.’
‘Six days,’ precisely, and not ‘in six.’
These holy, supernal days are called the days in which the Holy Name is included,
and they are included in it.
Happy is the portion of Israel above all the idol-worshipping nations,
for of them it is written: ‘You who cleave to Hashem your God
are all alive today.’”
First point. Rabbi Shimon says:
“You shall kindle no fire in all your dwellings.”
Fire is judgment (din).
Besides being a form of labor,
this labor in particular was singled out from the general rule:
the labor of kindling, because there is something special that it expresses.
Apart from being a labor, it expresses the special nature of the Sabbath.
For fire is judgment, and this day is a day of Atika Kadisha,
the exact opposite of judgment: a reality with no side of judgment in it at all.
That is why the Torah says, “You shall kindle no fire.”
It contradicts the essence of this day.
And if you say: but we see that lighting a fire on the altar is permitted,
for the communal offerings, which ascend to the Most High,
then we do see “it ascends to the Most High”: there, fire is indeed raised.
Offerings are placed there, something is burned,
fire is raised on the altar to the Most High.
There is something special here: we see in it a fire that consumes fire.
The fire of the altar comes to subdue the judgments, to sweeten them.
It is not itself judgment; it is a fire that consumes fire,
and it is what sweetens all the judgments. That is what this fire is about.
And precisely because of this, Atika Kadisha is revealed.
Atika Kadisha is revealed because of this essence of the Sabbath,
that it sweetens the judgments,
and Atika has the power to sweeten the judgments.
The Ramak (R. Moshe Cordovero) writes that Atika is revealed through Binah,
which is the root of the judgments.
Since Atika passes through Binah, Binah, the root of the judgments, sweetens them
and does not bring them out cut off from their source.
When fire is cut off from its source, it is harsh judgment.
But fire, too, can be connected to the source.
That is the fire on the altar, a fire that consumes fire;
it is what sweetens and elevates the judgments.
This is the special revelation of Atika Kadisha:
all is in joy, and judgment is absent on the Sabbath.
Then he cites, “For six days Hashem made,” and not “in six days.”
We have already seen this idea several times:
“six days” here does not speak of time. The days are the attributes, the sefirot,
the six sefirot of Zeir Anpin.
“Six days Hashem made”: not in six days; rather, six days are what Hashem made.
“Made” also means repair (tikkun).
These six days are really the creation itself, for each day has its sefirah:
the first day belongs to Chesed, the second to Gevurah.
“Six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth”:
heaven and earth are built of six days.
These are holy days, and the Holy Name is included in them all:
Zeir Anpin, Tiferet, which is the Name Havayah,
included in this Name, as the Name is in it.
Havayah in particular is bound up with these six sefirot,
which express the Name Havayah of Tiferet.
This is also the line, “Happy is the portion of Israel,” of whom it is written,
“You who cleave to Hashem your God.”
The Name Havayah, your God: you cleave to Hashem.
That is the point of Israel. Israel is Tiferet.
Tiferet itself is Tiferet; the Torah and the Holy One,
blessed be He, are all Tiferet.
This is the cleaving to Hashem, who is Tiferet,
by Israel, who are Tiferet, through the Torah, which is Tiferet,
and the six days, which are Tiferet. That is the verse that appears here:
“You who cleave to Hashem your God are all alive today.”
The life of Israel sweetens all the judgments and raises
everything to the Most High, in cleaving to Hashem.
That is the essence of it. Now let us look at two points.
[unclear] First, we said that Keter appears through Binah.
This is what the Ramak explains, and so everything is sweetened.
As for the special idea of “a fire that consumes fire,”
the one who discusses it at length is the Leshem.
We will read the end, and afterwards get to several passages.
One of the passages he writes is in Sefer HaDe'ah:
“All the clarifications (berurim) are like food,
from which the pure and fine is sifted out,
and it becomes flesh and blood in a person, and all his powers and his form.
So it is with all the clarifications:
all are a form of eating, wherever they ascend.”
Clarifications, every clarification made in all the worlds, are called “eating.”
For eating is really the form; this is why the Holy One,
blessed be He, created us as beings who eat:
through it we sift the good from the bad in the world.
We eat something; the waste is expelled, and the good remains.
Part of it [unclear] in the brain, and with it we study Torah and serve Hashem.
In effect, all of creation ascends through man.
This is called clarification (berur).
That is why the body has this sifting faculty, which can separate waste from food.
This is the point of clarification, and so every clarification is called eating.
That is the expression we saw here, “a fire that consumes fire.”
It is all a language of eating:
a fire that eats the fire and raises it to the Most High.
And so the Leshem explains this in another place as well, where he writes:
“‘Hashem your God’ is Malchut of Atzilut; she is a consuming fire:
‘Hashem your God is a consuming fire.’”
The expression “fire consuming fire” is built on this,
on what is written of Hashem your God: “a consuming fire.”
“She is a fire that consumes fire.
For by the power of the sweetened gevurot within her,
‘flames of love,’ she consumes the husks (kelipot) and the external forces,
and sifts out from them the sparks of holiness, which are the fire of the gevurot,
and consumes them, in the secret of ‘fire consuming fire.’
This is their ascent and entire repair: that they ascend in her.”
“Fire consuming fire” is the repair: the way that,
through eating, it raises, sifts and burns.
He explains this in the body as well, in eating itself.
Let us return to the passage we saw before, on eating. He writes:
“The order of the repair made in every food through eating is known:
it is done by the natural heat drawn from the elemental fire in the heart.
For the natural heat cooks the food and digests it in the stomach,
and then separates the waste and expels it, and sifts out its pure, fine essence,
and digests that too, and turns it into its own nature, blood and flesh,
which are the offspring and extension of the natural heat drawn from fire.”
In man, too, the whole concept of eating is “fire consuming fire.”
It is the concept of a consuming fire: the natural heat.
I don't know what natural scientists say about this today, but this is what he says.
It is drawn from [unclear], drawn from the power of the soul:
“Botzina de-Kardinuta,” a burning fire.
“This is all of man's vitality, clothed in the natural heat,
on which all his vitality depends.”
It is a fact that there is natural heat. Where does it come from?
It is an aspect of fire. Not fire with matches;
fire at its source is this quality of warming.
So heat is part of the faculty that makes these clarifications.
“…the essence: first it turns into blood and flesh,
then it generates the natural heat,
for the natural heat is the pure essence of man and his strength.”
He really sees this as the point, and this is the expression “fire consuming fire.”
He also writes about what was said of those angels,
the sparks mentioned, created on the second day,
[unclear] “a fire that consumes fire.”
This is the light of the supernal gevurot:
“they burn and consume all dross,
and refine and purify the sparks of all their filth,
and through this the sparks are clarified by them;
then, refined of all filth and scum, they are clarified and ascend.”
“The six days of creation,” he continues,
“are the six sefirot, Chesed to Yesod, of Zeir Anpin,
which shone into Malchut, and by them the world was created.
On the second day the sefirah of Gevurah ruled,
and the power of clarification was made and renewed on the second day of creation.”
This is connected to the angels.
He goes on to connect it to labor (melachah):
malachim (angels) and melachah (labor) are the same idea.
Labor, too, is a way of clarifying the sparks of holiness.
In the labors we do, too: we sow,
and the whole seed rots; only its elemental spark remains, and it grows.
The labors, too, are a way of clarifying things and transforming reality,
cleaning it so that it becomes a reality that is useful.
So much for this point.
Leshem Shevo VeAchlamah, in the Hakdamot; [unclear] here cites
what the author of the Leshem wrote.
What we read earlier was Sefer HaDe'ah; this is Hakdamot u-She'arim.
He says this: he speaks of four revelations in the world:
the revelation of Ein Sof, Tehiru Ila'ah,
then the world of Atzilut, and BYA (Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah).
These are the four stages.
“The fourth and fifth revelations, Atzilut and the worlds of BYA,
are His revelations, blessed be His Name, in the aspect of action.
For the first ones are in the aspect of will, thought and contemplation.
But the last revelations, the fourth and the fifth,
are His revelations that go out into actuality,
for in both of them His action was revealed. Therefore ‘making’ is written of both,
as it is written: ‘For six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth.’
It says ‘six,’ not ‘in six,’ for it refers to the six extremities of Atzilut,
which are the six days of creation.
So we find a language of making and action for Atzilut as well.”
“Six days Hashem made”: the six sefirot of Atzilut are also called “making,”
for from Atzilut there is an emergence into actuality,
a fuller revelation of things.
The language of “making”: so “six days” here, and not “in six,”
is not only about the words “six days” but also about the words “Hashem made”:
there is a making and a revelation here.
Zeir Anpin, the six days of Zeir Anpin:
there lies the main revelation, as we have already seen it written:
the main revelation of His Name is in Zeir Anpin, which is the main governance.
Then he says: this is called “six days,” the sefirot,
which bring forth from potential to actual the
supernal reality of the Name Hashem, the Name Elokim.
The sefirot bring it into revelation. That is the expression “six days Hashem made.”
That is what is special here. With Hashem's help.
